conclusion: APPROVE: ordinary approved Android selfsigned upload certificates pass without waiving strict verification, certificate policy, approved-fingerprint binding or TSA isolation. No remaining blocking defect identified in scoped diff.
reasoning: Actual JarFile signed payloads, not certificate display ordering, establish every signer identity. Full verified reads precede signers access. Unknown/unapproved/missing payload signers are rejected; ordinary META-INF files remain signed data.

Explicit selfsignature and full nonanchor PKIX leaf validation preserve validity, critical-extension and active certpath policy. Extra AlgorithmChecker uses exact JDK21 code-signing variant and applicable validation date; it is not a custom weaker allowlist.

Each distinct CodeSigner timestamp is checked with original JDK public roots and VAR_TSA_SERVER before its date is used. The upload trust store does not authorize a timestamp itself. Final strict jarsigner still verifies TSA/JAR metadata and manual signer purpose checks.

The helper creates only a CREATE_NEW public-certificate PKCS12 after validation. Final jarsigner success remains mandatory. Personal default keystore lookup is isolated. Nonselfsigned CA paths do not gain a newly trusted issuer/leaf.

Runtime.feature21 and scoped add-exports make internal API incompatibility fail closed. No dependency-verification, Gradle/application exports, app identity, publication state or candidate schema changes.

Tests consume the production shell fragment and real JDK21 source helper; invalid cases do not mock away signature verification. Wrong-ca test asserts real strict invocation exit4; stale-output test proves no overwrite/no later jarsigner. Positive test checks public trustedCertEntry and absence of PrivateKeyEntry.

The latest timeout regression starts an actual redirected TERM-resistant child, observes its attested PID/PGID, and verifies stopped/zombie/no-process status after group cleanup. run_owned now SIGKILLs its group in finally even if the leader exits during TERM grace; fixture also has independent last-resort owned cleanup.

RL-C1 input checks continue ahead of trust creation. Output signing_certificate_sha256 is assigned only after all actual signers agree and strict verification succeeds. This preserves the candidate fingerprint/digest fields used by existing RL-C3 promotion checks. Publication-disablement and collision guards are untouched.
counter_evidence: Not all certificate-pinning schemes are safe: importing the leaf alone bypasses critical checks. This fix explicitly validates leaf as a path element and isolates TSA roots, so that counterexample is addressed.
JarFile alone neither trusts certificates nor treats unsigned entries as an error. The implementation explicitly inspects CodeSigners and retains a separate strict verifier.
Data-bearing directory entries are skipped in helper streaming but are rejected by preserved downstream strict jarsigner logic Main.java838–842; helper skip is not an unsigned-data bypass.

Additional arbitrary embedded certificates do not become trusted. Exact JDK SignerInfo.getCertificateChain255–269 stops a self-issued leaf chain; nonselfsigned paths preserve original strict path behavior.
The original red Java-preparation expected77 failure is not an independent defect witness; the original approved-selfsigned positive case exit4 supplies the actual RL-C2 reproduction.

Generic private/custom ~/.keystore trust is deliberately no longer consulted, so no claim of compatibility with implicit personal trust additions is made. Approved selfsigned and ordinary JDK-public-CA policies are the supported release boundary.
